content_html:
We are ecstatic to announce that we have released the third alpha version of Pidgin 3.0!!! This release has an official version number of 2.97.0. We will continue releasing in this fashion until we are ready for 3.0.0 which will be the release we consider ready for end users. You can read more about our development phases here.

The release can still be found on SourceForge but we have a new CDN thanks to Fastly and the release can be found at fastly.imfreedom.org. It will also show up on Flathub Beta shortly.

If you don’t want to use the Flathub Beta method, there are build instructions in the README.md for building a Flatpak locally or installing into a meson devenv. Both methods avoid installing directly to your OS installation which is the preferred method as there is no easy way to uninstall the application at this time.

About

Just like the previous releases, this is a timed release. It is a snapshot of what we currently have and is something we think other tinkerers and developers may want to start playing with. But again, it is not meant for end users.

Most things are not implemented, the user interface has had little to no polish, and there are so, so many bugs. As such we are asking packagers to please not package this for your users at this time as the potential support requests will be too much for us to handle.

Highlights

This cycle has seen a lot of maintenance and not so many user facing changes, but there are a few to highlight!

New Presence Icons

The one and only Hylke Bons has graciously provided a new set of presence/status icons for us. You can see them in the contact list screenshot below. Sorry I forgot to include the offline user

Account Reconnection

Accounts will now automatically be reconnected after they get disconnected. This works on a simple static 1 minute timer between attempts right now and will probably be enhanced in the future. Unlike Pidgin 2 reconnection attempts will be made forever.

One of the cooler parts, is that this is now visible in the scheduler, which has not been polished at all as you can see below.

Message History

We finally created the PurpleHistory class which is how we represent messages in a conversation now. There is still a lot of work to do here, but protocols can now access this via the Purple.Conversation:history property to find messages as well as add additional.

There will be API in the future for the user interface to ask the protocol to load messages, but we aren’t quite there yet.

Plugins Dialog

We moved the plugins back to a separate dialog. It will probably get updated after some changes in GPlugin but you can take a look at it below.

Zulip

We removed the in-development tag from the Zulip protocol plugin. There is still a long way to go there, including adding support for channels, but DM’s have been stable enough that we felt comfortable removing the tag.

This means that it now shows up in the protocol list when creating a new account by default.

The full list of change can be found below.

Looking Forward

Alpha 4 is scheduled for 2026-10-29 and will have a version number of 2.98.0. We are moving from quarterly to monthly releases as we get closer and closer to a final release and have chosen the last Thursday of the month to be our release dates as historically Thursday night was our release night.

We have a bunch of tickets entered for Alpha 4 and you can keep an eye on the Burn down Chart for Alpha 4 to stay informed.

As always, priorities and possibilities can and will change, so even if something is listed for this release that doesn’t mean it will be in that release until it’s actually completed.

Thank You!

Thank you everyone for your continued support of Pidgin, it means a lot to us!

If you’re interested in contributing, you can check out our Contributing Guide to get started.

Also be sure to check out our merch store and if you’re feeling generous, you can donate to the project from our Donation Page.

content_html_zh:
We are ecstatic to announce that we have released the third alpha version of Pidgin 3.0!!! This release has an official version number of 2.97.0. We will continue releasing in this fashion until we are ready for 3.0.0 which will be the release we consider ready for end users. You can read more about our development phases here.

The release can still be found on SourceForge but we have a new CDN thanks to Fastly and the release can be found at fastly.imfreedom.org. It will also show up on Flathub Beta shortly.

If you don’t want to use the Flathub Beta method, there are build instructions in the README.md for building a Flatpak locally or installing into a meson devenv. Both methods avoid installing directly to your OS installation which is the preferred method as there is no easy way to uninstall the application at this time.

About

Just like the previous releases, this is a timed release. It is a snapshot of what we currently have and is something we think other tinkerers and developers may want to start playing with. But again, it is not meant for end users.

Most things are not implemented, the user interface has had little to no polish, and there are so, so many bugs. As such we are asking packagers to please not package this for your users at this time as the potential support requests will be too much for us to handle.

亮点

This cycle has seen a lot of maintenance and not so many user facing changes, but there are a few to highlight!

New Presence Icons

The one and only Hylke Bons has graciously provided a new set of presence/status icons for us. You can see them in the contact list screenshot below. Sorry I forgot to include the offline user

Account Reconnection

Accounts will now automatically be reconnected after they get disconnected. This works on a simple static 1 minute timer between attempts right now and will probably be enhanced in the future. Unlike Pidgin 2 reconnection attempts will be made forever.

One of the cooler parts, is that this is now visible in the scheduler, which has not been polished at all as you can see below.

Message History

We finally created the PurpleHistory class which is how we represent messages in a conversation now. There is still a lot of work to do here, but protocols can now access this via the Purple.Conversation:history property to find messages as well as add additional.

There will be API in the future for the user interface to ask the protocol to load messages, but we aren’t quite there yet.

Plugins Dialog

We moved the plugins back to a separate dialog. It will probably get updated after some changes in GPlugin but you can take a look at it below.

Zulip

We removed the in-development tag from the Zulip protocol plugin. There is still a long way to go there, including adding support for channels, but DM’s have been stable enough that we felt comfortable removing the tag.

This means that it now shows up in the protocol list when creating a new account by default.

ChangeLog

The full list of change can be found below.

期待

Alpha 4 is scheduled for 2026-10-29 and will have a version number of 2.98.0. We are moving from quarterly to monthly releases as we get closer and closer to a final release and have chosen the last Thursday of the month to be our release dates as historically Thursday night was our release night.

We have a bunch of tickets entered for Alpha 4 and you can keep an eye on the Burn down Chart for Alpha 4 to stay informed.

As always, priorities and possibilities can and will change, so even if something is listed for this release that doesn’t mean it will be in that release until it’s actually completed.

Thank you everyone for your continued support of Pidgin, it means a lot to us!
